fixtures.target_description: Slack window showing an internal check-in style conversation or message thread.
fixtures.primary_activity: Reading or participating in a Slack check-in conversation.
notes: This is an easy OCR-first baseline case.
Model output should stay grounded and not invent other apps or meetings.

fixtures.target_description: Browser-centric screen with Safari's iCloud tabs/start page on the left and a YouTube video page on the right.
fixtures.primary_activity: Browsing media content and Safari tabs.
notes: The menu bar shows Draw Things, but the visible windows are browser content.
This fixture should test the distinction between frontmost app and visible activity.

fixtures.target_description: Zoom Workplace meeting with participant strip visible above a Linear issues view.
fixtures.primary_activity: Participating in a Zoom meeting while viewing Linear issues.
notes: A good result may mention both Zoom and Linear.
Misclassifying this as generic browser research is a failure.

fixtures.target_description: Cursor editor workspace with development controls and terminal-related UI elements.
fixtures.primary_activity: Editing code or working in a development environment.
notes: A good result should prefer coding/development language.
Mentioning unrelated meetings is a hallucination.

fixtures.target_description: Linear issues list in a browser with a Zoom participant sidebar on the right.
fixtures.primary_activity: Reviewing or managing work items while on a Zoom call.
notes: A good result should identify Linear/work tracking as the main visible content.
This is different from the YouTube/browser fixture and should not collapse into generic browsing.
